Two callers, neither reads the result: Game_PitLane_ApplyPitstopTyres passes 1 (mov dl,1 at 0x1434bdd9d, call at 0x1434bdd9f) and afterwards calls pitstopComplete 0x142e94780 (0x1434bde3f) whether or not this ran; Game_PitBoxCarActor_Update passes 0 (xor edx,edx at 0x1403c8dd1, call at 0x1403c8dd3). The body finds the next set by the id at +0x9c70 among the 0x18-byte entries from +0x9bd0 (count +0x9c48). When it differs from the fitted set (+0x9938 id, +0x9940, +0x9948) it logs the second line and then, with pit_stop set, calls 0x142e96390 (0x142e941f2) instead of storing the set at +0x9938..+0x9948 itself (0x142e9421d..0x142e94231). It then calls 0x142ea1d30, ORs dword +0x208 & 0x1f of every tyre record (records at +0x30, stride 0xde0, count u64 +0x98d0; 0x142e94280..0x142e9428a) into ebp, calls 0x142e83130(record, k, 0, 0) for k = 0..4 on every record (0x142e942cb..0x142e943ce), runs the per-record calls 0x142e83130/0x142e87870/0x142e87ab0 on the selected record with those bits and byte +0x9915 (0x142e944f7..0x142e946a8), calls 0x142ea2300(component, 1, 0x101) and returns 0 (xor eax,eax at 0x142e946bc, its one exit). pitstopComplete (a jmp to 0x14f43e230) clears +0x9910 and calls 0x142e83130/0x142e87540 only on the +0x4a0 and +0x940 sub-records of each tyre record, for k = 0..5 (log 'MOX/Tyres: pitstopComplete() disabling everything but set %d').
